meta.scope: Three representative camera sensors (full frame, APS-C, Micro Four Thirds) with cited, evidence-labeled parameters, plus generic sensor-physics facts. See research/sensor-sources.md for prose notes, conflicts and the reasoning behind each sensor pick.
openProblems: Per-ISO read noise in electrons (base ISO and above the DCG switch) could not be extracted for any of the three chosen camera sensors: photonstophotos.net's RN_e.htm/PDR.htm charts are JS-rendered and returned no numeric text to this session's WebFetch tool, and several DPReview forum threads that discuss/quote that data returned HTTP 403. Chart/thread URLs are recorded as pointers in each record. Whoever can load photonstophotos.net interactively (or has a DPReview-authenticated fetch path) should fill these in directly rather than via a second-hand search summary.

The MFT record (OM-1 / E-M1 III) leans on web-search-summarized numbers for its full-well and DCG-switch-ISO figures more than the other two records, for the same reason above. Flagged low-confidence in that record.

Chip identity is confirmed by primary Sony datasheet + strong community consensus only for the full-frame pick (a7R IV / IMX455), and even there one conflicting "IMX451" mention was found and not resolved. APS-C and MFT records explicitly do NOT claim their vendor pixel-level figures (IMX571, IMX294) are the exact chips in the named cameras -- they are same-format Sony sensors used as documented stand-ins, clearly labeled throughout.

Per-channel (R/G/B) QE curves were not obtained as numbers for any of the three sensors; every vendor/maker source publishes these only as graph images, which this pass could not read (per the task's instruction to say so and move on rather than guess).

Dark current at realistic in-camera operating temperature is only directly measured (by vendors) for the cooled astro-camera implementations at 0C/-20C; the Tj=60C in-camera estimate for the full-frame record is explicitly a derived extrapolation, not a measurement.

chipIdentity.note: Sony does not publicly state which camera uses IMX455. The identification is a widely repeated community finding (multiple outlets, and a Sony-Semiconductor datasheet whose pixel count/pitch/diagonal match the a7R IV exactly: 9576x6388 effective pixels, 3.76um pitch, 43.3mm diagonal). One search result surfaced a conflicting teardown label "IMX451AQL" for the a7R IV; that discrepancy is unresolved here and flagged for the lead. Where a figure below comes from the Sony IMX455 datasheet or a ZWO/QHY product using that same chip, it describes the silicon family, not a Sony statement about the a7R IV specifically.

derivedAtTj60C.loc: derived from the 0C vendor figure using the generic doubling-temperature relation (see generic.darkCurrent), extrapolated to Tj=60C, the junction temperature Sony's own IMX455 datasheet uses as its characteristic-spec reference condition
derivedAtTj60C.calc: v(Tj) = v(0C) * 2^((Tj-0)/Tdouble), Tdouble = 6.5C (midpoint of the 5-8C generic range) => 0.0017 * 2^(60/6.5) = 0.0017 * ~601 = ~1.02 e-/s/pix. This is a rough order-of-magnitude estimate, not a measured in-camera figure: an uncooled mirrorless body's actual sensor operating temperature varies with ambient, session length and stabilization/video load.

isoInvarianceMeasurement.procedure: Shoot the same scene twice at the same aperture and shutter speed: once at a high ISO (correctly exposed in-camera), once at a low ISO (deliberately underexposed by the same number of stops the ISO was raised). Push the low-ISO raw file's exposure in post-processing by that same stop count so both frames match in brightness, then compare shadow noise and detail. A sensor is "ISO-invariant" over a given range when the two results are visually indistinguishable -- i.e. raising in-camera analog gain (ISO) buys nothing over digital exposure push once the signal is past the sensor's DCG-switch/read-noise floor.
